## Personality

A remarkably capable and hardworking individual, she excels at managing both her own concerns and those of others around her. Recognized as a kind and clever soul, she displays a deeply gentle and skillful nursing ability, serving as a patient, tender, and unwearied caregiver to her sick husband. She is famously outspoken and prides herself on speaking her mind without fear or favor, though others view her as a critical, meddlesome gossip who does not spare people when enumerating their shortcomings. Compulsively strict and corrective, she enjoys being asked for advice and maintains strong opinions, including a prejudice against [Americans](../codex/factions.md#american), political enthusiasm, and a profound skepticism toward both higher education for women and fiction writing. Practical by nature, she spends the leisure of her old age knitting cotton-warp quilts.

## History

Mrs. Rachel [Lynde](../character/lynde.md) lived as a long-time neighbor to [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), having raised ten children, buried two, and knitted sixteen cotton warp quilts. Eight years prior to [Anne](../character/anne.md) Shirley's arrival, she and her husband mortgaged their farm to start their youngest boy in the west. When she first learned of Marilla's plan to adopt an orphan, Mrs. Rachel expressed strong disapproval and warned her of the risks involved. She later visited [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) and insulted Anne's appearance, which provoked an angry outburst from the young girl; however, she completely forgiven [Anne](../character/anne.md) after receiving a dramatic apology. Mrs. Rachel continued to offer practical counsel, such as advising [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) to let [Anne](../character/anne.md) stay home from school until she cooled down after a punishment, and keeping the household informed of local news and gossip. Following the death of her husband [Thomas](../character/thomas-lynde.md), Mrs. Rachel moved into [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) to live with [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md), allowing [Anne](../character/anne.md) to leave her teaching post and attend [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college). ## Quotes

> "But really, Green Gables doesn’t seem as out of the world as it used to do . . . Anne has lots of company and the twins make it real lively. And anyhow, I’d rather live at the bottom of a well than leave Avonlea."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v2 XXVI Around the Bend P27](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0027)

> "and as for the twins, I’ll be glad to do all I can for them; but I won’t undertake to answer Davy’s questions, that’s what. I’m not an encyclopedia, neither am I a Philadelphia lawyer. You’ll miss Anne for that."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v2 XXVI Around the Bend P29](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0029)

> "I never saw her look so pleasant before, that’s what. Well, there weren’t many tears shed over her, poor old soul. The Elisha Wrights are thankful to be rid of her, and I can’t say I blame them a mite."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v3 ch.Evening P11](../source/v03-c28.md#nw-v03-c28-p0011)

> "though, mind you, there was a time I didn’t think so—that evening I came up to see Anne and she treated us to such a scene. Many things have changed since then, that’s what."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v4 CHAPTER 2 THE HOUSE OF DREAMS P2](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0002)

> "She’s terrible skinny and homely, Marilla. Come here, child, and let me have a look at you. Lawful heart, did any one ever see such freckles? And hair as red as carrots! Come here, child, I say."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014)

## Relationships

### [Anne](../character/anne.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne--rachel-lynde.md)

Mrs. Rachel [Lynde](../character/lynde.md) and [Anne](../character/anne.md) initial met on bad terms after Rachel insulted Anne's appearance, driving [Anne](../character/anne.md) into a furious tirade. However, after [Anne](../character/anne.md) dramatically apologized, Rachel completely forgave her and offered comforting words about her hair. Over time, their relationship evolved into a warm friendship where Rachel serves as a well-meaning neighbor and advisor to [Anne](../character/anne.md) as she grows up.

- Enemy of — insulted Anne and faced intense mutual hostility  _(ended v1)_  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified P16](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0016)</sub>
- Friend of — well-meaning older neighbour and advisor (since v2)  <sub>[v2 I An Irate Neighbor P54](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0054)</sub>

### [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/marilla-cuthbert--rachel-lynde.md)

Rachel Lynde and [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) share a longstanding neighborly friendship. Rachel frequently visits [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) to trade news, offer pragmatic advice regarding household matters, and discuss local community affairs. Though Rachel initially expressed strong disapproval and warned [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) against adopting an orphan, [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) continues to rely on her as a trusted confidante.

### [Emily](../character/emily.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/emily--rachel-lynde.md)
